title: CobaltBridge Connector & RefArch lab sync
topics: Helm operator vs plain Helm chart
summary: Redwood + CobaltBridge alignment on marketplace connector packaging, security gating (KMS, audit logs), and an in-lab benchmark plan. Decided to pursue a hybrid listing with a Helm operator for lifecycle, run two focused benchmarks (throughput + latency) and validate KMS keywrap flow in dev VPC. Action items and owner commitments captured; next call to review benchmark artifacts and draft marketplace listing doc.
questions: Can we support customer-managed KMS for keys used in Private deployment?
How will canary routing pick model variants when quantized models produce small quality drops?
What telemetry is required by marketplace to show usage/billing?
next_steps: Jordan to send reserved capacity estimator and draft listing checklist by 2026-07-22
Priya to run benchmark with CobaltBridge sample dataset and share logs by 2026-07-27
Maya/Evan to provision dev VPC and KMS test key by 2026-07-24 and share access details

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 1h 15m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Maya (CobaltBridge Head of Cloud), Evan (Platform Eng), Lina (Security), Tomas (DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan Ellis: alright, uh hi everyone thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the account. we wanted to run through a hands-on lab style sync for the marketplace connector and reference architecture. we'll cover packaging, vpc/kms, and a short benchmark plan. Priya, Marco you wanna intro?

[00:18] Priya Nair: yep hi all, Priya here. I'm the solutions engineer who will run the bench and help with operator packaging. hello Maya, Lina, nice to meet you.

[00:28] Maya Patel: hey thanks. appreciate the time. we've got some constraints to flag early: we need customer-managed keys for production, and our security team wants as little control-plane data in Redwood cloud as possible. also timeline is tight — marketplace listing by mid-august if possible.

[00:45] Marco Chen: got it. quick clarifying q — by customer-managed keys you mean you want a KMS key in your AWS account and Redwood to use a keywrap flow, right?

[00:53] Maya Patel: exactly, keywrap is the preferred pattern. plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.

[01:02] Priya Nair: we support both customer KMS and Redwood-managed KMS. for the private deployment listing we can wire the keywrap and show the flow — there's a sample runbook. small caveat on operator: the Helm operator needs a role with EKS IRSA permissions for the KMS calls, if you're using that flow.

[01:20] Evan Ortiz: ok, we run EKS in account, IRSA is fine. what's the risk surface? is the entire traffic egressing to Redwood's control plane?

[01:30] Jordan Ellis: good q. for the hybrid marketplace listing we propose a split control plane: listing metadata and billing is in Redwood cloud, but inference traffic in private deployment stays in your VPC. there is a short-lived registration handshake to exchange the signed attest and token, after that tokens rotate locally. so network egress is minimal.

[01:52] Dr. Lina Sousa: can we see audit logs for that handshake? our audit requirements require at least 365 days retention of auth events.

[02:01] Priya Nair: yes — we can export auth/audit events to your S3 bucket or push to your SIEM via a Kinesis/Firehose integration. retention and encryption at rest uses your S3 and KMS.

[02:17] Tomás Ruiz: if we go with Helm operator, how is upgrades handled? we like automated rollouts and rollback hooks.

[02:25] Marco Chen: operator handles lifecycle — canary upgrades are supported via labels and rollout strategy in the operator. you can define thresholds for latency and error budget; operator will rollback to previous revision on regressions. just be aware canary behavior depends on model variant compatibility, e.g. quantized variant may slightly differ.

[02:45] Maya Patel: that brings up the quality question — quantization often reduces model size but can alter outputs a bit. how do you recommend balancing cost vs quality for marketplace customers?

[02:57] Priya Nair: typical pattern: offer two variants in listing — a quantized cost-optimized variant and a full-precision variant. use canary routing to run a small percentage of traffic to full-precision to monitor regression via eval set. Redwood Optimize provides delta alerts tied to your prompts.

[03:17] Evan Ortiz: can we wire that into our telemetry? we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency.

[03:25] Jordan Ellis: yep we'll expose per-route dashboards. marketplace listing requires exporting metering records — we'll provide a connector that writes usage events (tokens, route ids) to the marketplace billing endpoint. important: timestamps must be UTC and idempotent event ids.

[03:42] Dr. Lina Sousa: curious on encryption in transit — are TLS termination points within our VPC for private inference?

[03:50] Priya Nair: yes, inference endpoints terminate within your VPC; only the control-plane handshake touches Redwood control plane. TLS mutual auth optional for the control channel if you want stronger mTLS.

[04:03] Tomás Ruiz: about packaging — you mentioned Helm operator vs plain Helm. pros/cons?

[04:09] Marco Chen: operator adds lifecycle features (canary, auto-rollback, automated credential rotation). plain Helm is lighter-weight for teams that manage upgrades themselves. since CobaltBridge wants automated rollouts and canary routing, operator is preferable. operator does add an extra manifest, CRD, and a small controller image to run in-cluster.

[04:29] Maya Patel: can we see an example values.yaml and the operator CRD?

[04:34] Priya Nair: yes — I'll share a values.yaml tailored to your EKS setup, and a sample CRD for the model listing. I'll include kustomize overlays if you want to keep cluster-level differences.

[04:45] Evan Ortiz: bench plan — what will you measure? throughput, p95 latency, cold-starts?

[04:52] Priya Nair: we'll do three experiments: sustained throughput with 8-16 concurrent streams to measure tokens/sec and GPU utilization; 99th and 95th percentile latency with varying context lengths; and cold-start times for scaled-down pools. sample payloads from CobaltBridge will be used to better reflect your prompts.

[05:12] Maya Patel: are you going to test quantized models too?

[05:16] Priya Nair: yes — we'll include quantized model variants (8-bit + int4 where supported) to capture delta on latency and token cost. note: some kernels behave differently on older GPU nodes; we'll call out hardware mapping in the bench report.

[05:30] Tomás Ruiz: on the market listing side, what's required for the initial submission?

[05:35] Jordan Ellis: minimal listing for hybrid pattern needs: product description, reference architecture diagram, deployment manifest (Helm/operator), security checklist (SOC2 evidence links), sample benchmark report, and packaging for the marketplace connector including metering hook. we can provide a template listing doc.

[05:51] Dr. Lina Sousa: SOC2 evidence — we won't upload our raw audit reports to Redwood, what's the intake pattern?

[05:58] Marco Chen: we offer a vendor intake portal where you attach redacted artifacts or point to a secure location. for SOC2 we often accept a CSP-signed attestation plus a scoped control summary. we can also provide proofs of encryption and keywrap flow in the lab.

[06:13] Evan Ortiz: any known incompatibilities to watch for with our EKS version (1.27)?

[06:20] Priya Nair: operator supports EKS 1.24 through 1.28; CRDs are backwards compatible but we'll validate RBAC and admission webhook versions. if you use custom CNI plugins there may be minor networking adjustments for metrics scraping, but nothing blocking.

[06:36] Maya Patel: timeline sanity check — if we provision dev VPC and KMS by next Friday, how long until you have bench results?

[06:44] Priya Nair: two business weeks for full bench and a writeup — so if you provide access by 2026-07-24 we should be able to deliver by 2026-07-27 (fast track) or by 2026-07-30 for fuller analysis.

[06:57] Jordan Ellis: for pricing, I'll run a reserved capacity estimator based on your expected qps; send the expected peak tokens/sec and we'll produce scenarios (hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid).

[07:10] Tomás Ruiz: any special telemetry or metering hooks we need to add to the operator?

[07:15] Marco Chen: the operator emits usage events to a local forwarder which batches and sends to the marketplace metering endpoint. you'll need an endpoint secret and a service account with network egress permission. batching thresholds can be tuned to balance latency vs throughput.

[07:31] Dr. Lina Sousa: legal/procurement note — marketplace contracts require indemnity clauses and data residency statements. can Redwood accept EU data residency for EU customers?

[07:41] Jordan Ellis: yes — we have EU regions and can pin customer data and logs to EU-only regions for listings targeted at EU customers. legal can provide the template redlines — I'll include a contact.

[07:53] Priya Nair: quick demo note — after the bench we can show a live canary and rollback, but we'll run that in your dev cluster to avoid any production risk.

[08:03] Maya Patel: sounds good. also, can you include a short script to sanity-check inference outputs between quantized and fp16 so our data team can run automatic quality checks?

[08:12] Priya Nair: yes, we'll share an eval harness that calculates embedding similarity and a thin prompt-regression test. it'll output a CSV with diffs and a pass/fail threshold.

[08:24] Evan Ortiz: one more: billing lines — we need daily metering exports so finance can reconcile. is daily push supported?

[08:30] Jordan Ellis: daily push is supported; we can also provide S3 export or push to your billing endpoint. event format is newline-delimited JSON with fields: event_id, timestamp, tokens_consumed, route_id, customer_id. I'll attach schema.

[08:46] Tomás Ruiz: ok, wrapping up, can we confirm owners and dates?

[08:50] Jordan Ellis: yes — action items as follows. I'll send the reserved capacity estimator and listing template by 2026-07-22. Priya will run the bench and share by 2026-07-27. Maya to provision VPC/KMS by 2026-07-24. Tomas to share Helm values 2026-07-23. Lina to send compliance checklist by 2026-07-26.

[09:10] Maya Patel: fine by me. thanks everyone. this was helpful.

[09:15] Jordan Ellis: great — we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the bench review week of 2026-07-28. thanks all.

End of transcript.
